title: ER-luminal [Ca2+] regulation of InsP3 receptor gating mediated by an ER-luminal peripheral Ca2+-binding protein
abstract: Modulating cytoplasmic Ca 2+ concentration ([Ca 2+ ] i ) by endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-localized inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor (InsP 3 R) Ca 2+ -release channels is a universal signaling pathway that regulates numerous cell-physiological processes. Whereas much is known regarding regulation of InsP 3 R activity by cytoplasmic ligands and processes, its regulation by ER-luminal Ca 2+ concentration ([Ca 2+ ] ER ) is poorly understood and controversial. We discovered that the InsP 3 R is regulated by a peripheral membrane-associated ER-luminal protein that strongly inhibits the channel in the presence of high, physiological [Ca 2+ ] ER . The widely-expressed Ca 2+ -binding protein annexin A1 (ANXA1) is present in the nuclear envelope lumen and, through interaction with a luminal region of the channel, can modify high-[Ca 2+ ] ER inhibition of InsP 3 R activity. Genetic knockdown of ANXA1 expression enhanced global and local elementary InsP 3 -mediated Ca 2+ signaling events. Thus, [Ca 2+ ] ER is a major regulator of InsP 3 R channel activity and InsP 3 R-mediated [Ca 2+ ] i signaling in cells by controlling an interaction of the channel with a peripheral membrane-associated Ca 2+ -binding protein, likely ANXA1.
